_comment: form: theropod|raptor|ceratopsian|stegosaur|sauropod|pterosaur|hadrosaur|ankylosaur|tinybird|budgie. len/height are in world units (about 0.5 m each).

base.name: Tyrannosaurus rex
facts: Tyrannosaurus rex lived about 68 to 66 million years ago in what is now western North America.
Its bite force was among the strongest of any land animal ever, enough to crunch bone.
Juvenile tyrannosaurs were slender and fast; they bulked up in a teenage growth spurt.
Our T. rex has a faint plume of purple fuzz along the spine. Fossil relatives such as Yutyrannus show real feathers.

base.name: Triceratops horridus
facts: Triceratops means three-horned face. The frill protected the neck and may have been used for display.
Its beak was perfect for snipping tough ferns and cycads.
Thousands of Triceratops fossils have been found, making it one of the best known dinosaurs.

base.name: Stegosaurus stenops
facts: The plates along its back were full of blood vessels and probably worked for display and temperature control.
Its brain was about the size of a lime, yet it thrived for millions of years.
The tail spikes are nicknamed the thagomizer, after a Far Side cartoon.

base.name: Brontosaurus excelsus
facts: Brontosaurus means thunder lizard. It was briefly thought to be a mistake, then restored as a genus in 2015.
It could swallow plants whole and rely on gizzard stones to grind them.
Our lagoon helps the big sauropods rest their joints. They love to wade.

base.name: Pteranodon longiceps
facts: Pteranodon is technically a pterosaur, a flying reptile cousin of the dinosaurs. Our staff call them dino-adjacent.
Its wingspan could reach over six meters, and it had no teeth.
Pterosaurs had a pycnofiber fuzz, a hairlike covering.

base.name: Anchiornis huxleyi
facts: Anchiornis huxleyi was about the size of a pigeon and lived about 160 million years ago in China.
Fossil melanosomes show black and white body feathers, with a reddish-brown crest.
It had flight feathers on both its arms and its legs: four wings!
Anchiornis loves Brazil nuts. Ask the stand attendant for a scoop.

base.name: Melopsittacus undulatus
facts: Budgerigars are living dinosaurs: every bird descends from small feathered theropods.
Wild budgies are green and yellow. Blue, white and violet came from captive breeding.
The zebra stripes on the head and back are called barring, and the cheek patches are violet.
Parakeets in flocks chatter constantly, and they preen each other's heads.

rediscovered.name: Velociraptor mongoliensis
facts: Velociraptor was turkey sized and fully feathered. Quill knobs on its forearm bone prove it.
The famous film version was about twice the size of the real animal.

rediscovered.name: Parasaurolophus walkeri
facts: The hollow crest worked like a trombone, resonating low calls through the forest.
It could walk on two legs or four.

rediscovered.name: Gallimimus bullatus
facts: Gallimimus means chicken mimic. It was one of the fastest dinosaurs, probably ostrich-like at 50 km/h.

rediscovered.name: Ankylosaurus magniventris
facts: Ankylosaurus had bony eyelids, armor plates, and a tail club that could break bone.

rediscovered.name: Microraptor gui
facts: Microraptor had four wings and glossy, iridescent black plumage. It could glide between trees.

rediscovered.name: Dilophosaurus wetherilli
facts: The twin crests were thin and delicate, probably for display. There is no evidence it spat venom.

rediscovered.name: Pachycephalosaurus wyomingensis
facts: Its skull dome was up to 25 cm thick. Whether it headbutted rivals is still debated.

rediscovered.name: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus
facts: Spinosaurus had a sail, paddle-like tail and crocodile-like jaws. It hunted in rivers.
